summary: ANTIRUG area S1 batch (22-19 Task 3, D-16 area-batch tier), presented together once the ANTIRUG slice audit, thresholds and cards were complete. Six S1 entries, each a way a rug could go unnoticed or the emergency sell could fail, be suppressed or go through the wrong router under a realistic condition: AUD-ANTIRUG-001 (RC-13, STRAND) three reconnect paths (anti-rug handleWsClose, one bot.ts loop per DEX, dashboard onRestart) each rewrite ctx.wsProvider, so the rug-log subscription can vanish after a dashboard stop, be duplicated after a reconnect, or be left on a provider nothing destroys (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:916-944, :643-657; src/bot.ts:1552-1576, :1593-1618; src/api/routes/chains.ts; card OD-11); AUD-ANTIRUG-002 (independent, STRAND) a WebSocket reconnect attempt that cannot connect kills the bot: no socket has an error listener and src has no uncaughtException handler, so the ws library's error event is thrown and the process exits before any reconnect alert can fire; reproduced on localhost (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:916-944, :945-980; src/bot.ts:1561, :1603; src/utils/provider.ts:37; card OD-11); AUD-ANTIRUG-003 (independent, STRAND, candidate) the circuit breaker counts dispatches, not rugs: every matching log of one LP removal starts its own confirm gate and exit attempt and refused duplicates still count, so one rug can trip the chain breaker and suppress every later anti-rug exit on that chain (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1341-1396, :628-637, :1964-1983; src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:240; card ANTIRUG-01); AUD-ANTIRUG-004 (independent, STRAND) a refused, timed-out or failed anti-rug escape is never retried by the detector: nothing records the unsafe verdict, re-triggering needs a new LP log, and the poll timer the escape cleared comes back only on some failure paths; this also confirms by code reading the mechanism AUD-EXIT-014 left as a candidate (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1832-1842, :1900-1907, :1850, :1871-1882; src/anti-rug/exitTrigger.ts:240; card EXIT-11); AUD-ANTIRUG-005 (independent, STRAND) backfill does not do what its contract says: it fires live exits through the evaluator, replays already-handled windows on every registration, and after a long healthy session any reconnect exceeds the maximum window so the real outage is never replayed (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1146-1159, :713-718, :1018; card ANTIRUG-02); AUD-ANTIRUG-011 (independent, STRAND) after a restart anti-rug re-registers each position with the first dex of its pool type, not the dex it was bought on, so a position on a chain's second V2 dex gets its emergency exit routed through the wrong router (src/bot.ts:2096-2098; src/utils/db.ts:612-621; src/anti-rug/detector.ts:397-406; card EXIT-10; the anti-rug side of the defect AUD-EXIT-013 records for the exit monitor, presented here as its own entry; any merge is for the 22-28 consolidation). No S0, no rail, test-origin-db-row or non-public-secret item, and no rediscovery of an already-escalated item was found in the ANTIRUG slice. The bot is OFF for all of v7.0, so none of these can cause a loss now. Nothing is changed in Phase 22 (NAC-13): each item is proven with a real-path test in Phase 23 and fixed in Phase 24. The operator was asked to acknowledge and say whether any item needs its own urgent decimal phase before Phase 24, or to stop the phase.

ruling_note: Interpretation recorded as relayed by the orchestrator: the operator chose the acknowledge-continue option for all six S1 entries. No severity was changed, no decimal phase is inserted, and Phase 22 continues. Context, attributed to the 22-19 executor and the execute-phase orchestrator and NOT to the operator: the executor named AUD-ANTIRUG-002 (a refused reconnect crashes the process, reproduced on localhost) as the strongest candidate for a decimal phase; the orchestrator recommended acknowledge-continue because the bot stays off until the end of v7.0, and noted that AUD-ANTIRUG-002 is already proven and should be among the first Phase 24 fixes. As S1 capital findings, none of these can rest on a keep-current default; each blocks the live re-entry gate until it is fixed.
